summary: Dependency-confusion squat with install-time host beacon to OOB collectors
details: @myorder-frontend-commons/analytics@0.2.0 is a public npm package squatting an internal-looking scope. package.json wires preinstall, install, and postinstall to `node poc.js`, which collects host-identifying data (hostname, OS username, platform/arch/release, cwd, node version, package version, lifecycle trigger, and names of present CI environment variables) and transmits it to attacker-controlled out-of-band collectors over HTTP GET and as a hex-encoded DNS label — specifically db4jftohu4noreqdanngpnb3ger45ykrt.oast.fun and 80-190-83-27.nip.io. The shipped index.js is an inert stub exporting function names (getOrderIds, getOfferIds, isOrderPaid, isSmartDelivery, etc.) chosen to mirror an internal package so that a build which resolves this public package in place of a private one does not crash. This is the canonical dependency-confusion exploitation shape: an install-time reconnaissance beacon that confirms resolution of the squatted name inside a victim's build environment and leaks host and CI identifiers to third-party infrastructure. An in-source comment framing the behavior as 'authorized security research' is author-controlled text and does not change the installer-facing effect.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
